extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners (and applicants/practitioners) on evaluating, processing, and documenting amendments and other replies filed after final rejection or after allowance, including use of form paragraphs, reasons for non-entry, expedited processing, and 37 CFR 1.312 rule applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for nonentry of amendment (concise)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasons for nonentry should be concisely expressed. Examples given: (A) amendment would not avoid any of the rejections set forth in the last Office action and thus would not place the case in condition for allowance or better condition for appeal; (B) amendment would raise the issue of new matter; (C) amended claims present new issues requiring further consideration or search; (D) amendment presents additional claims without canceling any finally rejected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily the specific deficiencies need not be discussed but reasons should be concise and may use the example wordings (A)–(D). When an amendment is denied entry, follow with the appropriate explanatory form paragraphs (7.72–7.80) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate status of each claim and which proposed claims would be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment, and which proposed claims would be entered on filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an amendment is entered for appeal purposes, indicate which individual rejection(s) set forth in the action from which the appeal was taken would be used to reject the new or amended claim(s). Use form paragraphs (e.g., 7.69, 7.70 and their .01 variants) to show Allowed claim(s): [ ], Rejected claim(s): [ ], Claim(s) objected to: [ ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify applicant when portions would be acceptable or render claims allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should be notified if certain portions of the amendment would be acceptable as placing some of the claims in better form for appeal or complying with objections or requirements as to form; similarly inform applicant if the proposed amendment to some claims would render them allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aids filing of a brief consistent with claims as amended. Include a statement that the final rejection stands and that the statutory period runs from the date of the final rejection when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PTOL-303 for advisory action after final when reply doesn't place application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply from applicant after final rejection where such reply is prior to filing of an appeal and does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form advises applicant of disposition of proposed amendments and of the effect of any argument or affidavit not placing the application in condition for allowance or which could not be made allowable by a telephone call to clear up minor matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectations for examiner responses to amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from receipt by the examiner. A reply to an amendment after final rejection should be mailed within 30 days of the date the amendment is received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is placed in condition for allowance, promptly notify applicant by Notice of Allowability form PTOL-37. If delays are expected (e.g., extensive examiner’s amendment), notify applicant via interview and mail Examiner Initiated Interview Summary PTOL-413>B. Every effort should be made to mail the letter before the period for reply expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for lack of appeal or corrective amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that filing a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply. See MPEP § 1207 for appeal and post-appeal procedure; see §§ 715.09 and 716 for after final practice relative to affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set statutory period and use correct form paragraph heading (7.67 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.67 (and variants 7.67.01, 7.67.02) as a heading in advisory actions prior to appeal to set the period for reply and indicate whether the shortened statutory period (SSP) applies or is extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate variable language in brackets (e.g., --continues-- or --is extended--, and the full statutory period such as --FOUR-- months). Use 7.67.01 if first reply filed within two months; use 7.67.02 when no variable SSP set in final, etc. Do not use these for reexamination proceedings. Follow with form paragraph 7.41.01 if transitional provisions of 37 CFR 1.129(a) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendment will be entered for appeal purposes, state proposed rejections (7.69.01/7.70.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: See 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2): include proposed rejection(s) that would be detailed in the Examiner’s Answer if applicant elects to file an appeal. To be complete, such rejection(s) must be addressed in any brief on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.69.01 or 7.70.01 to state: 'Claim(s) [1] would be rejected for the reasons set forth in [2] of the final Office action mailed [3].' Identify grouped claims and link to paragraph number or statement of rejection (e.g., 35 U.S.C. § 103 based upon A in view of B). Repeat for each group subject to the same rejection(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment denied entry because 'lacks showing why necessary and not earlier presented' (7.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.72 when 'There is no convincing showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) why the proposed amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this paragraph as the sole reason for refusing entry unless the situation is aggravated, in which case provide a full explanation. Follow with form paragraph 7.41.01 where transitional provisions of 37 CFR 1.129(a) apply if not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment denied entry because it 'raises new issues' requiring further consideration or search (7.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.73 when 'The proposed amendment raises new issues that would require further consideration and/or search.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify the new issues including questions of new matter; examples are sufficient if new issues are extensive. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment denied entry because it does not improve form for appeal (7.75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.75 when 'The proposed amendment is not deemed to place the application in better form for appeal by materially simplifying the issues for appeal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraph 7.71. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment denied entry because additional claims presented without canceling finally rejected claims (7.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.76 when 'The proposed amendment presents additional claims without canceling a corresponding number of finally rejected claims.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by 7.71. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform when proposed new claims would be allowable if filed separately (7.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.78: 'Claim [1] as proposed would be allowable if submitted in a separately filed amendment canceling all non-allowed claims.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.71. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously. This informs applicant of a path to allowance via separate amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/exhibit/request considered but does not overcome rejection (7.79)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.79: 'The [1] has been entered and considered but does not overcome the rejection because [2].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede by appropriate heading (7.67 series or 7.68). In bracket 1 insert --affidavit--, --declaration--, --exhibit--, or --request for reconsideration-- and provide an explanation in bracket 2. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/exhibit not considered due to lack of good and sufficient reasons earlier presented (7.80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.80: 'The [1] will not be considered because good and sufficient reasons why it was not earlier presented have not been shown. [2]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede by 7.67 series or 7.68. In bracket 1 insert appropriate label and include an explanation in bracket 2. Follow with 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply and not used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing for replies under 37 CFR 1.116 (marking and handling requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use expedited procedure, amendment or reply under 37 CFR 1.116 must be marked 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' on the upper right of the paper and the envelope must be marked 'Box AF' in the lower left corner. If mailed, envelope should contain only replies under 1.116 and be addressed to 'Box AF, Assistant Commissioner for Patents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked papers are specially processed by the Mail Center, forwarded to the TC and expedited to examiner via SPE; goal is to mail examiner’s action within 1 month of receipt. If no action within goal + normal mailing time, applicant should call SPE and, if necessary, TC Director. Applicants should use the markings (bright color preferred) to obtain benefit; delays attributable to applicant (delayed interviews, petitions, etc.) will prevent achieving the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand delivery acceptance criteria at Technology Center
rubrics_metrics.description: TC will accept a personally delivered paper only if: (1) the paper is accompanied by some form of receipt which can be handed back to the person delivering the paper; and (2) the examining group being asked to receive the paper is responsible for acting on the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt may be a card with identifying data (applicant name(s), application number, filing date, description of paper). The paper and receipt are date stamped with the TC date stamp; receipt returned to deliverer. If fees or deposit account charges present, TC personnel will hand-carry papers to Office of Finance for processing and then enter into file wrappers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution closed after allowance (Ex parte Quayle) and use of Quayle action
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims in an application have been allowed, prosecution of the application on the merits is closed even though there may be outstanding formal objections which preclude fully closing the prosecution (Ex parte Quayle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments touching the merits are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection. Use form paragraph 7.51 (Quayle Action) to notify applicant that application is in condition for allowance except for formal matters, that prosecution on the merits is closed, and set shortened statutory period for reply (TWO MONTHS).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 amendments after allowance: timing and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance; any amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee and may be entered on recommendation of the primary examiner approved by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'amendments' under 1.312 include: (A) an amendment to the specification, (B) a change in the drawings, (C) an amendment to the claims, (D) a change in the inventorship, (E) the submission of prior art. Primary examiners have delegated authority to recommend entry; supplemental reissue oaths are treated as amendments and must comply with 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of primary examiner authority for 1.312 entries
rubrics_metrics.description: After Notice of Allowance, the application is technically no longer under primary examiner jurisdiction, but the primary examiner may make examiner’s amendments and enter amendments that merely correct formal matters in the specification or drawing or formal matters in a claim without changing its scope, or cancel claims, without forwarding to the SPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments other than trivial formal corrections require SPE approval. TC Director establishes policy on trivial informalities based on two vital formal requirements: (A) disclosure must be adequately clear, and (B) any invention present be defined with sufficient clarity to form an adequate basis for an enforceable contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria for 1.312 amendments affecting disclosure, scope, or adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarks accompanying an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 that affect the disclosure, change scope of any claim, or add a claim must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution continuation is not permitted by 1.312. If recommendation is against entry, a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and brief reason usually suffices. Provide detailed statement only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons against entry under 1.312 (sufficient grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate reasons for non-entry under 1.312 include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims added by 1.312 are dependent-type, usual non-entry reasons are less likely to apply, although issues of new matter, sufficiency of disclosure, or undue multiplicity could still arise. A brief statement is usually adequate when recommending against entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean claim set and parenthetical guidance for post-allowance submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of an entire clean set of claims is construed as directing cancellation of all previous versions of any pending claims. When rewriting a claim in a clean set, parenthetical expressions from the claim to be rewritten should not be repeated in the clean set; parenthetical expressions should appear in the clean set only when a claim is being amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provides a clean set with no underlining/bracketing and is not making changes, a marked up version should not be submitted. Any claim not accompanied by a marked up version constitutes assertion that it has not been modified relative to the immediate prior version. Examiner has no responsibility to ensure accuracy of applicant’s claim rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments allowed after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid; 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the issue fee date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.10 (Amendment Filed After the Payment of Issue Fee, Not Entered) to notify applicant and include the date of the amendment in the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims after allowance entry not matter of right (714.16(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment received after notice of allowance includes one or more claims copied or substantially copied from a patent, entry of those copied patent claims is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific procedure in MPEP § 2305.04 when such copied claims are received. Additional fee requirements may apply (see MPEP § 607 and § 714.16(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed with motion under 37 CFR 1.633: entry conditioned on motion grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment filed with a motion under 37 CFR 1.633(c)(2) applies to an application in issue, the amendment is not entered unless and until the motion has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter such amendments until the underlying motion is decided in applicant’s favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees required when amendment adds claims beyond paid number
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required (see MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and notation of 1.312 amendments by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 affecting disclosure, adding claims, or changing scope are sent to Publishing Division which forwards them to the Technology Center that allowed the application; the examiner promptly considers the amendment and indicates 'Enter — 312', 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink in the upper left corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If class/subclass transfers occurred after allowance, the amendment may be transmitted to another TC and the original examiner consulted. Prompt consideration and clear entry notation by examiner are required.
